chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fadhdhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) — meaning the First — who said:
I heard him saying: 'Whoever pays the zakat on his wealth completely and places it in its (appropriate) place will not be asked on the Day of Judgment from where he earned his wealth.'

key_terms.تَامَّة: Complete, full — emphasizing that the zakat must be paid in the correct amount without reduction
key_terms.زَكَاة: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax on wealth, one of the five pillars of Islam; here emphasizing 'complete' zakat (tammah)
key_terms.مَوْضِعِهَا: Its appropriate place — refers to the eight categories of zakat recipients mentioned in Quran 9:60

ai.seo_question: Does paying complete zakat absolve a person from being questioned about their wealth on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) declares that complete fulfillment of zakat — both in amount and in proper distribution — absolves a person from accountability regarding the source of their wealth on the Day of Judgment. This hadith was transmitted in the context of early Islamic jurisprudence concerning the consequences of fulfilling financial religious obligations. The teaching addresses concerns about the legitimacy of wealth accumulation, assuring that diligent payment of zakat purifies one's wealth entirely.
